method: A single anonymised hand-off of 176 PNGs named with 16 hex characters. The identifier read handoff/READ-ME-FIRST.txt and nothing else from the tree, answered every render one at a time while looking at it, and committed the answers (sha256 96ad8b4ccab2c16d6ae509b4305453136ad7b4b8e81c07c7a3b78500fe5915fa) BEFORE running reveal. The feature audit was made afterwards with the contract open, against the same renders. Seven audit entries first filed as UNCHECKABLE were resolved rather than left standing: three by direct observation (every character figure faces the direction it travels) and four by measurement with ImageMagick - streetcar body 792x290 px = 2.73:1 against a contract target of about 2.7; Peggys Cove light 396x866 px with a 230 px red top = 0.27 of height and 2.19 base widths tall; city wall left edge at x=49, 41 and 35 for rows 80, 200 and 300, so the wall is wider at the foot and the batter is real.
supersedes: 6.1.0, in full. That record was carried into this tree with its results, scope and narrative intact while verify-art record replaced only runIntegrity and handoffRun, so it stated 35 pass / 17 fail / 2 not-checked over a handoffRun that scores 42 / 12 / 0. scope.unrenderedIsNotAVerdict: Neither subject was handed over and neither is audited here. Both are UNRENDERED BY DECISION: their renders would be repeating, droppable parallax tiles that the art bible forbids putting an identifying feature on, so a verifier able to name Ottawa or Quebec City from them would be reporting a defect. An audit of an image nobody was shown would be the quietest kind of false pass, and the scorer fails one on purpose.
scope.countsAreDerived: Every number here is what scripts/lib/art-score.mjs reports for this record over the tree it is committed into: scored 42/54 subjects, over 176/176 renders whose art is unchanged since the verdict, 57 gating and 119 diagnostic, 287 mustBeRight features confirmed present, 0 uncheckable, 0 not re-checked because the art moved, 2 unrendered by decision.

runIntegrity.blindnessCaveat: partial - TWO leaks are declared in primingLeak, and the second of them was missing from the superseded record. Neither was sought and both were visible before any render was opened.
whatIsProven: The 176 identifications in handoffRun.answers were written from image bytes alone, under opaque 16-hex names, with no filename, label, contract or reference photograph in view.

They were hashed by verify-art commit BEFORE verify-art reveal opened the keymap, and score re-checked the hash against the file on disk. It matched. The blind pass was not revised with the answer key open.
Every source digest in the keymap was re-derived against the tree this record is committed into and every one matched: 176 of 176 renders are unchanged since the verdict, so no verdict here is stale.
whatIsNotProven: That the identifier read nothing outside the hand-off directory. Only the hand-off can give that; what can honestly be said is stated in primingLeak.
That the small rungs of the size ladder measure recognition. The same identifier saw the full-size render of each subject first, so a w140 answer measures retention of what was already recognised.
That any render is ACCURATE. Recognisable and accurate are different properties (docs/art-verification-method.md).
runIntegrity.whatThisDoesNotEstablish: Scoring proves a stated verdict matches the contract. It cannot prove the verdict was made blind; only the hand-off gives that, and only if the identifier did not go and look. The one thing visible before the answers were fixed is declared in primingLeak.

Rows touched by either leak carry primed. Beyond these two: no subject contract, no filename, no art bible, no level document, no asset manifest and no harness library was opened until after commit and reveal.
